prediction.likelyOutcome: Caton is more likely than not to prevail on the threshold liability question given the Trust's own fifth-amendment admission that the Section 1(b) conditions could not be satisfied, which cuts against the Trust's argument that no obligation ever ripened absent exercise; the $314,000 option-consideration refund should follow close to in full if liability is found. The $128,885.50 out-of-pocket expense component is meaningfully weaker given reliance on deposition testimony rather than documentary proof, and is likely to be reduced or contested at trial even in a liability win for Caton.

issues.label: Refund of Option Consideration ($314,000) -- Core Liability and Primary Damages Component
Evidentiary Sufficiency of Deposition-Only Damages Proof
Timing of Termination Notice (Two Days Before Option Expiration)

outcome.description: The circuit court granted Caton summary judgment on a futility theory and awarded him $442,885.50 in damages (the full amount of his demand) plus $96,329.00 in attorneys' fees. The Court of Appeals of Virginia affirmed that the agreement required Caton to exercise the option, but reversed the summary judgment award of damages and fees because futility was not established as a matter of law, and remanded for further proceedings.
outcome.finalNote: Summary judgment reversed and remanded; no final figure yet.
